correctness.rationale: The ordinary (closed-neighborhood) domination criterion was derived directly from the tensor adjacency. Three disjoint incidence edges always dominate; otherwise Koenig matching-cover theorem restricts selected cells to at most two covering row/column lines. Each of the one-line, mixed-cover, same-side-cover cases was resolved with necessary and sufficient tests, boundary restrictions m,n>=2, and deletion witnesses. Five disjoint families produce the exact polynomial. Verification independently enumerated all subsets in eleven small cases (1,419,077 candidates) and confirmed 2,231 minimal sets and every coefficient, plus generated-only tests in five larger cases. Finite tests are corroborative only.

evidence: Defant-Iyer Theorem 2.1 supplies ordinary minimum domination for two factors; Proposition 4.5 handles upper domination with a four-cell reduction, but no exact family count.
Anderson-Kuenzel-Rall Theorem 3 addresses well-dominated direct products.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Previously known extremal numbers, well-dominated classification, and unimodality are strictly weaker statements about the desired inclusion-minimal cardinality coefficients. The known total-domination classification on identical graphs has open-neighborhood quantifiers, so does not imply ordinary-minimal classification.

originality.rationale: Full-text section comparison against Defant-Iyer 2017 (minimum and upper parameter), Anderson-Kuenzel-Rall 2019 (well-dominated characterization), and Burcroff-O'Brien 2021 (all-set polynomial unimodality), together with focused mathematical-literature and OEIS searches, did not identify the complete ordinary-minimal five-family enumerator. A known total-domination result for this same product is logically distinct and does not give its ordinary-minimal family. Priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The ordinary minimal dominating sets are a natural antichain for a classical graph-product domination problem already studied for its extremal invariants and all-set polynomial. The result classifies every labeled solution at arbitrary unequal factor sizes, gives all coefficients, and proves an unbounded forbidden interval in the minimal-set cardinality spectrum for K3 × Kn. This is not a renaming of upper/lower domination or a numeric small-case count.
